plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, PLTU) to zero.
Exit high-beta software names (METU, MSFU) to reduce risk.
Trim QQQI to 20% to address concentration and favor income.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation by reducing leverage and volatile assets.
A significant cash buffer will be maintained, leading to lower expected monthly returns.
Stops will be kept tight to limit potential losses.
conservative.read: This conservative approach aims for lower, steadier monthly gains around 1.5% by significantly reducing leverage and focusing on income and broad market exposure. The primary risk is missing out on potential upside if the market rallies strongly.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta software (METU, MSFU) to small positions.
Introduce VRT as a new position based on strong scanner signals.
This plan balances risk reduction with selective growth opportunities.
It aims for moderate monthly returns of approximately 2.5% by blending index exposure with quality tech.
A moderate cash buffer will be held, and overall leverage will be managed carefully.
Focus remains on risk-first growth.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% monthly growth by reducing exposure to the riskiest leveraged ETFs and high-beta software, while adding a promising new name (VRT). The risk is that the market moves against the remaining concentrated tech positions, and the new addition may not perform as expected.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) and high-beta software (METU, MSFU) to target growth.
Add VRT as a new position, concentrating exposure in high-conviction names.
This plan aggressively pursues growth by increasing leverage and concentration.
It aims for higher monthly returns around 4%, but with significantly increased drawdown risk.
Leveraged ETF decay and daily rebalancing are key risks to monitor.
Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for high growth (around 4% monthly) by increasing leverage and concentrating in tech and leveraged ETFs, including adding VRT. The significant risk is amplified drawdowns, potential margin calls, and the compounding effects of leveraged ETF decay, requiring very strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs and high-beta software positions to zero.
Increase QQQI allocation to 30% to maximize income generation.
This plan prioritizes generating steady monthly income over capital appreciation.
It aims for lower, consistent monthly distributions, accepting lower growth potential.
The focus is on capital preservation and reliable income streams.
NAV can still decline in market downturns, despite income focus.
income.read: This income-focused plan aims for consistent monthly distributions around 1% by shifting heavily into QQQI and exiting all leveraged and high-beta tech. The risk is that market downturns can still reduce the Net Asset Value (NAV) of holdings, and distributions are not guaranteed and can vary.
